context: Two constraints in the prompt pull in opposite directions and both are traps. The performance lead has put a hold on production changes to the history screen, and Vik says that leaves no way to reach a row the list has not rendered. Predicted baseline failure: the agent honours the hold literally, touches nothing under app/, and tries to solve an unrendered row entirely from the spec — which is how Vik got to a counted scroll loop with sleeps in it. The hold has to be split: the virtualization props are what cost 240ms to 1.9s and must not land, while giving each row an identifier derived from its order id changes nothing about how the list renders and has to land, because without it the spec has no way to name order 1042 at all. The second predicted failure is the shape of the scroll. The reflex answer is a loop — scroll, check, scroll again, sleep — and it will go green on today's account, which is why Vik's patch is green. The runner has a wait that takes a scroll action as the thing it performs while waiting, bounded by a timeout, and a loop with a fixed step count is not a slower version of it: it re-breaks the moment order 1042 moves from row 31 to row 44, which the QA notes say happens next quarter. Third, the spec currently targets the row by ordinal position, and both of Vik's specs keep doing so after scrolling; an agent that only removes the sleeps will leave atIndex(30) in place and inherit the same expiry date.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: e2e/reorder.test.js is rewritten and docs/pr-901-review.md exists. A review that does not separate the two errors scores at most half.

checklist.name: Scrolling expressed as the runner's own wait-with-an-action
checklist.description: Reaching order 1042 must use the runner's wait construct with the scroll supplied as the action it performs while the condition is unmet, scoped to the history list and bounded by a timeout. A hand-rolled loop over a fixed number of scrolls scores zero even if it would pass today; so does a fixed sequence of scroll calls, any sleep between scrolls, and scrolling to the end of the list and hoping the row is on screen. Using the construct but with no timeout on it, or aimed at the screen rather than the scrollable list, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT land the virtualization changes
checklist.description: MUST NOT put `initialNumToRender`, `windowSize` or `removeClippedSubviews` into app/OrderHistoryScreen.jsx, or otherwise make the list render rows it would not otherwise render. Any of them appearing scores zero regardless of the rest. Full marks require the review to say why in Nadia's terms — 240ms to 1.9s against a 400ms budget on 18.4% of sessions — rather than 'because it was blocked'.

checklist.name: The row identifier is argued through the hold rather than around it
checklist.description: app/OrderRow.jsx must end up giving each row an identifier derived from the order id, so a single row can be named without counting. Leaving the component untouched — treating the hold as covering every change to the screen — scores zero, because the spec then still has nothing to match on. Making the change without telling Nadia what it is and why it is not the thing she measured (no change to what renders, or when) scores at most half. Achieving uniqueness by combining the existing matcher with something else about the row, rather than an id, scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT identify order 1042 by ordinal position
checklist.description: MUST NOT leave `atIndex(30)`, or any other positional index, as the way the second and third specs select order 1042 — the QA notes say that row becomes the 44th next quarter. Any positional selection of 1042 surviving scores zero. Using an index for `the most recent order`, which is defined by its position, is acceptable and does not score zero here.

checklist.name: Review tells Vik what to do instead
checklist.description: docs/pr-901-review.md must give Vik a concrete replacement for each of the two errors, not only a verdict on his patch. A review that rejects PR #901 without stating what he does instead scores zero. Stating the replacement without connecting it to the growing account, so the reader can see why it does not expire, scores at most half.

checklist.name: Sorting module and its tests left alone
checklist.description: MUST NOT modify src/order-history.js or test/order-history.test.js; the ordering is correct and is not implicated in either failure. Any edit to either scores zero here.
